title: Introduction to NLP
description: Turn text into representations and evaluate language tasks carefully.
prerequisites: Python data handling and model evaluation.
objectives: Choose a text representation and baseline
Recognize leakage and language-specific failure cases
explanation: Natural language processing covers tasks such as classification, extraction, search, translation, and generation. Define what the output should contain and how correctness will be assessed. A short fixed-label classifier may be easier to validate than an unrestricted generated answer.

A bag-of-words representation counts terms while discarding most order. TF-IDF weights terms using their frequency within documents and across a corpus. Fit the vocabulary and any corpus statistics on training data. Contextual embeddings can capture richer patterns, but cost more and still need evaluation.

Preserve information deliberately. Removing punctuation, negation, or accents may change meaning. Evaluate languages, misspellings, long inputs, and ambiguous cases separately. Deduplicate templates and group related messages before splitting so near-identical text does not inflate held-out results.

terms.definition: Dividing text into units used by a representation.
The terms or tokens recognized by an encoding.
A text weighting scheme using term frequency and document frequency.

example: A support team labels messages billing, technical, or unclear. A term-count baseline is cheap to inspect. Include both “payment failed” and “payment did not fail” to reveal whether the representation loses a distinction that matters.
mistakes: Removing negation as an unimportant word.
Learning vocabulary from the final test set.
Assuming one language result applies to every language.
exercise: Write twelve invented support messages including ambiguity and negation. Define labels, a template-aware split, and a count-based baseline. Identify three cases where word order or context changes the correct label.

questions.question: What information does a basic bag-of-words representation mostly discard?
questions.answer: Word order, while retaining term occurrence information.

questions.question: Where should a text vectorizer learn its vocabulary?
questions.answer: On the training partition before transforming evaluation data.
questions.distractor: On every future test message first.

questions.question: Why might removing the word “not” damage a sentiment classifier?
questions.answer: Negation can reverse the meaning of the phrase being classified.
questions.distractor: All short words always increase sentiment accuracy.

questions.question: Does a contextual embedding eliminate the need for text evaluation?
questions.answer: No. It changes the representation but still has task and distribution limitations.

questions.question: How should repeated support templates be split?
questions.answer: Group related or near-duplicate templates to reduce cross-split leakage.
questions.distractor: Place identical copies in both training and test sets.
